title: pvThreshold
body:
## pvThreshold

Extracts the cells whose values of a chosen point or cell array satisfy a criterion (Between LowerThreshold and UpperThreshold, below the lower or above the upper), producing an unstructured grid (or a masked hyper tree grid). It exposes the full native control: component handling for vector arrays (one component, magnitude, All or Any), Invert, AllScalars for point data and a continuous cell range. Use threshold for the common inclusive range test with validated field names; use pvClip with a scalar clip for smooth cuts through cells.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Cells are kept or dropped whole; the boundary is staircase-shaped, not interpolated.
- With a point array and AllScalars true (ParaView default), a cell is kept only if all its points pass; set AllScalars false to keep cells touching the range.
- LowerThreshold and UpperThreshold may be initialized from the array range by ParaView; set both explicitly.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Threshold`. Identity: `filters/Threshold`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Threshold filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). The input needs at least one point- or cell-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AllScalars` | If the value of this property is 1, then a cell is only included in the output if the value of the selected array for all its points is within the threshold. This is only relevant when thresholding by a point-centered array. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ComponentMode` | This property specifies how multi-component arrays are handled. 'Selected' will use the 'Selected Component' property. 'All' will pass if all components satisfy the rule. 'Any' will pass if any component satisfies the rule. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Selected","All","Any"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Selected"` |
| `Invert` | Invert the threshold results. That is, cells that would have been in the output with this option off are excluded, while cells that would have been excluded from the output are included. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `LowerThreshold` | The value of this property specifies the lower bound of the thresholding operation. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `MemoryStrategy` | Select how to construct the result in memory: - MaskInput (default): shallow copy the input and mask all cells being thresholded - Regenerate Trees And Index Fields: generate a new tree structure but use indexed arrays on the input for cell data - New HyperTreeGrid: construct a new HyperTreeGrid from scratch representing the minimal threshold of the input | `{"type":"enum","values":["Mask Input","Regenerate Trees And Index Fields","New HyperTreeGrid"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Mask Input"` |
| `Scalars` | The value of this property contains the name of the array from which to perform thresholding. Be aware that HTG does not support multi-component arrays. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `SelectedComponent` | This property specifies which component of the array needs to satisfy the rule. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ThresholdMethod` | This property indicates the threshold method. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Between","Below Lower Threshold","Above Upper Threshold"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Between"` |
| `UpperThreshold` | The value of this property specifies the upper bound of the thresholding operation. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `UseContinuousCellRange` | If off, the vertex scalars are treated as a discrete set. If on, they are treated as a continuous interval over the minimum and maximum. One important "on" use case: When setting lower and upper threshold equal to some value and turning AllScalars off, the results are cells containing the isosurface for that value. WARNING: Whether on or off, for higher order input, the filter will not give accurate results. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

  "mode": "serial",

}

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvThreshold",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
